ranking_note: Authored from the before descriptions at commit 968bfeb77df9416c9dd074ed9de3c7ac4f4049a7, frozen before the rewrite; protocol per /playbooks:skill-authoring ## Measurement. Competitors are event-storming:simulation (AI agents playing personas to run a workshop, usually on a Miro board, plus evaluating, retro and bounded-context discovery against an existing board), planning:design (types, contracts and module boundaries resolved before a plan; its listing says 'model this domain'), architecture:map-events (async message topology read from committed C# code), architecture:map-context (C4 system context from tracked configuration), domain-driven-design:curate-language (maintaining the ubiquitous-language glossary), prototype:pressure-test (a throwaway app stepping business rules through awkward event sequences) and planning:brainstorm (diverging into candidate approaches before scope is locked). methodology owns EventStorming facilitation knowledge and reference, and choosing and planning a format for a workshop that humans run.

Give me a cheat sheet of event storming vocabulary: hotspot, read model, external system and the rest.
We have two hours with the claims experts on Thursday. Help me choose a workshop style and draft the agenda.
